title: Selling a Houston House With a Sewer-Line Problem
description: Selling a Houston house with backups or a damaged sewer line? Identify the likely boundary, document the scope and compare repair with an as-is sale.

faq.q: Can I sell a Houston house with a sewer-line problem?
faq.a: Yes. First document what is known, whether the suspected problem is on a private or public segment, and what the buyer is agreeing to accept. A repair, traditional listing and current-condition cash sale carry different costs and timing.

faq.q: Does a sewer camera inspection prove the exact repair cost?
faq.a: No. It can document observed conditions and location under its scope, but access, excavation, pipe length, permits and additional findings can change a repair proposal. Ask for the recording and written interpretation.

faq.q: Is every sewer backup the City of Houston's responsibility?
faq.a: No. Houston Public Works distinguishes public pipes and right-of-way issues from private-line blockages. Verify the actual location and service provider because municipal, utility-district and private-system boundaries can differ.

faq.q: Does selling as-is mean I can ignore a known sewer issue?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Texas disclosure requirements and exemptions depend on the facts and transaction. Describe known conditions honestly and get professional advice when needed.
